name: trace
description: Trace turns any UI screenshot into a live, editable React component. Gemini vision detection mapped to your design-system catalog, rendered in-browser and scored for accessibility.

paragraphs: Paste a screenshot. Get a real, runnable React component.

A draftsman plotter loading sequence narrates the wait (detecting, grounding, drafting, checking accessibility), and the whole app wears a deliberate precision-drafting look: vellum, graphite, and vermilion, reticle frames, dimension annotations, Space Grotesk and Public Sans.
features: Design-system grounding. Generation is constrained to a real component catalog (an in-prompt whitelist), so Trace reuses actual components and variants instead of inventing generic markup. No vector database, no…

Trace lines. Animated draftsman construction lines wire each region of the screenshot to its inspector row to its place in the preview, with bidirectional hover-to-locate. The name is literal: you can see which part of…

"What the AI sees" inspector with honest confidence. Every detected element gets a numbered bounding box on the screenshot, a mapped component and variant, a confidence reading, and an honest grounding tag: grounded,…
Live, editable preview. The component renders in a Sandpack sandbox (Tailwind via CDN) you can edit in place, not a static screenshot of code.
Self-repair loop. Generated code is compile-checked and auto-fixed by re-prompting on failure. Runtime errors in the preview get a one-click "Ask Trace to fix it" that re-prompts with the error.
